name: Rodan
label: Quarterstick
lede: Three years, one album cut in four weeks, and four members who spent the next two decades starting other bands.

eras.title: A failed rap project
eras.text: Two Louisville friends who had been at this since high school start a band, get through a name change and two drummers, and land on a bassist who will define the sound as much as either guitarist.

years.src: Touch and Go: Rodan · AllMusic: Rodan biography · Wikipedia: Rodan (band) · Paste: Rodan
years.h: [[Jason Noble|1a30edd1-b7ee-4d9f-ae1c-af8cd4759718]] and [[Jeff Mueller|06502a8d-ae1a-4ca4-ab28-07fa3582597e]] start Rodan with Tara Jane O'Neil
years.p: Noble and Mueller met in high school and art school; Touch and Go says the band grew out of a failed high school rap project. [[Tara Jane O'Neil|a9a6334c-1541-4aef-8092-fe743f0df64f]] plays bass, and [[Jon Cook|e7024639-8b66-4aff-a30f-d6484699b5b8]] is first behind the drums.
years.xp:
AllMusic says the group first called itself Kinkhead International before taking Rodan, after the Japanese monster-movie creature. Wikipedia lists two drummers before the permanent one: Cook and John Weiss, both in 1992.

Paste describes 1992 demos of Shiner and Tooth Fairy Retribution Manifesto, both of which end up on the album, as a band still working inside the strictures of hardcore punk.

eras.title: Prototypes and a month in Chicago
eras.text: The band puts out a cassette, a record and a compilation track, gets a permanent drummer, then spends four weeks in September and October making the album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rodan (band) · Touch and Go: Rodan
years.h: Kevin Coultas takes the drum stool; a cassette and a 7-inch appear
years.p: [[Kevin Coultas|49a21bcb-7fe5-4218-87c9-073a5b344413]] joins in 1993. That year the band self-releases the Aviary cassette demo, puts out How the Winter Was Passed on Three Little Girls, and gives Darjeeling to a Simple Machines compilation.
years.xp: Sources disagree on the format of How the Winter Was Passed: Wikipedia calls it an EP, the Louisville Hardcore History wiki lists a 7-inch. Darjeeling appeared on The Machines: 1990-1993, from Simple Machines.

years.h: Four weeks in Chicago and Louisville to record Rusty
years.p: Six songs, cut between September 25 and October 22, 1993. Engineers were Steve Good, [[Slint|2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28]]'s Brian McMahan and [[Bob Weston|7364260a-0a3e-4a6c-bcf8-b4e743c0b2c0]] of [[Shellac|604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea]].
years.xp: Wikipedia credits the album to producers Jake Loewenstein and the band, and says sessions were split between Chicago and Louisville. Wikipedia's Rodan page names Weston as the producer. The sources do not say which songs were cut where.

eras.title: Rusty, and out
eras.text: The album lands in April, the band turns up in a movie, records for John Peel, and calls it quits by autumn.

q: This is an album to readily get lost in.
years.src: Wikipedia: Rusty · Prefix: Quarantining the Past · Sun 13: Everything Changes
years.h: Rusty arrives on Quarterstick: six songs, one album
years.p: Rodan's only full-length runs six songs, with The Everyday World of Bodies the longest at just over six minutes.
years.xp:
Bible Silver Corner opens it; Shiner, Jungle Jim, Gauge and Tooth Fairy Retribution Manifesto fill it out. It came out on Quarterstick, the Touch and Go sister label, and AllMusic gave it five stars.

Fact magazine put it fifth on its 2016 list of the best post-rock albums. Prefix wrote that Rodan made one full record, with a quick final note, and that was it.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tara Jane O'Neil · Tiny Mix Tapes: RIP Jon Cook · Wikipedia: Rodan (band)
years.h: Half-Cocked puts the band in the movie theater
years.p: In the 1994 indie road movie, O'Neil plays herself, credited as Rhonda, and Cook acts. Rodan's Tron ends up on the 1995 Matador soundtrack.

years.src: Sun 13: Engine Roar · Paste: Rodan · Touch and Go: Fifteen Quiet Years
years.h: Rodan plays its last show, and nobody is sure which night
years.p: Mueller says the band's final show was September 23 or 24, 1994, and that June of 44 got going in Brooklyn two months later.
years.xp:
Mueller told Sun 13: our last show was, I think, September 23 or September 24 of 1994. Wikipedia and Touch and Go both date the breakup to 1995 and the end of the year respectively, so the date above is Mueller's own account.

The band's BBC session for John Peel, three songs, was recorded in 1994 per Paste and Touch and Go, and shows up on the 2013 compilation.

eras.title: Everybody gets a band
eras.text: Four members become four scenes. Mueller heads to Brooklyn and June of 44, Noble builds Shipping News with him and keeps Rachel's going, O'Neil and Coultas keep making records with other people.

years.src: Wikipedia: June of 44 · Sun 13: Engine Roar
years.p: It started in Brooklyn, per Mueller, with [[Jeff Mueller|06502a8d-ae1a-4ca4-ab28-07fa3582597e]] on guitar and vocals, and Quarterstick released Engine Takes to the Water that year.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists June of 44's members as Fred Erskine, Sean Meadows, Mueller and Doug Scharin, and says the group drew people from Rodan, Lungfish, Rex and Hoover. The band took its name from the period when Henry Miller and Anais Nin corresponded.

years.p: Noble's chamber ensemble, founded in Louisville in 1991 with Rachel Grimes and Christian Frederickson, puts out its first album that year. Coultas also played in Rachel's, per Sun 13.

years.h: Tara Jane O'Neil's other bands: [[Retsin|398e10c3-ed3c-424d-a607-3c346b31afa2]] and [[The Sonora Pine|357563d2-56a6-451a-8d0b-19cc8c904a75]]
years.p: Retsin, with Cynthia Nelson, put out Salt Lick on Simple Machines in 1995 and Egg Fusion in 1996. O'Neil and Coultas make two Sonora Pine albums before it ends in 1997.

years.h: Noble and Mueller start [[Shipping News|d6ed84da-0414-4c44-ace7-ae491ce7d999]] to score a radio show
years.p: They first write music for the Chicago-based NPR program This American Life. Save Everything follows on Quarterstick in 1997.
years.xp: The band took its name from E. Annie Proulx's 1993 novel. Kyle Crabtree joined on drums, and Todd Cook was added on bass in 2004.

eras.title: The box
eras.text: Noble, Mueller and Weston remaster the recordings, Noble dies, and the survivors finish the compilation.

years.src: Louisville Public Media: Musician Jason Noble Dies · Rolling Stone: Rodan Singer Jason Noble Dead · Wikipedia: Shipping News
years.p: The Louisville Public Media report and Rolling Stone both say Noble died in Bethesda, Maryland, of synovial sarcoma, diagnosed in 2009.
years.xp: LPM reports he died at the National Institutes of Health while in a clinical trial of an experimental treatment. He had worked at the Louisville record store ear X-Tacy and written music criticism for LEO. Shipping News effectively ended with his death.

years.src: Touch and Go: Fifteen Quiet Years · Paste: Rodan
years.h: Fifteen Quiet Years collects everything else Rodan cut
years.p: Nine studio tracks, including the Peel session and out-of-print singles, plus ten live tracks from the band's archives.
years.xp:
Bob Weston, Mueller and Noble remastered the recordings in 2009 at Chicago Mastering Service. Noble helped design the packaging and pick the live tracks; Mueller letterpress-printed the vinyl and CD packaging at his Dexterity Press studio.

Paste says the release was delayed by the BBC dragging its feet on licensing the Peel tracks, and that the surviving members are letting the recordings speak for the band, with no reunion planned.

eras.title: The tapes from Baltimore
eras.text: Tapes made before Rusty are found, digitized and released for charity.

years.src: Bandcamp: The Hat Factory 93 · Tiny Mix Tapes: RIP Jon Cook
years.h: Hat Factory '93: prototypes of the Rusty songs
years.p: Recorded in the first half of 1993 at the Hat Factory in Baltimore by Forrest (Tony) French and released 26 years later, with proceeds going to Girls Rock Louisville.
years.xp:
Adam Reach rescued the original tapes and transferred them in 2015, and Keven Ratterman remixed and mastered them in 2019. Cook plays drums on these tapes; Coultas plays on later recordings.

Cook died on February 9, 2013 after a long illness, at age 40, according to Tiny Mix Tapes.
